topic: Mastering the Cross Product: From 2D intuition to 3D mechanics

sections.title: Prerequisite & The 2D 'Pseudo-Scalar'
lecture_lines: 2D cross product measures signed parallelogram area.
It indicates rotation direction: clockwise or counter-clockwise.
It represents the perpendicularity of two vectors.
animations: Create 2D coordinate plane with vectors u and v. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Label vector u in #FF6666 and vector v in #66CCFF.
Show 2D parallelogram formed by vectors u and v using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg].

sections.title: The 3D Definition: Creating Space
lecture_lines: 3D cross product creates a new perpendicular vector.
Use the Right-Hand Rule to find direction.
Curl fingers from A to B; thumb points result.
animations: Create 3D coordinate space with vectors a, b, c. (Color: #FFFFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hand.svg]
Show 3D parallelepiped formed by vectors a, b, c. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hand.svg]

sections.title: The Algebraic Formula (The Determinant)
lecture_lines: We use a 3x3 determinant to compute it.
Basis vectors i, j, k define the frame.
Cross-multiplication calculates the x, y, z components.
animations: Display 3x3 matrix M with entries a, b, c. (Color: #FFFFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

sections.title: Geometric Meaning & Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Formula: magnitude of A times B times sin theta.
Physics application: Torque equals r cross F.
